questions.prompt: Which organelle releases most of a cell's usable energy (ATP)?
questions.hint: It is often called the powerhouse of the cell.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and make most of the cell's ATP.

questions.prompt: Plant cells have a cell wall, but animal cells do not.
questions.hint: Think about what keeps a plant stem stiff.
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall. Animal cells have only a cell membrane.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell holds most of its DNA?
questions.hint: It acts like the control center.
questions.explanation: The nucleus stores the cell's DNA and controls the cell's activities.

questions.prompt: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.hint: Every living thing is made of at least one.
questions.explanation: The cell is the smallest unit that can carry out the functions of life.

questions.prompt: What do we call the jelly-like fluid inside a cell?
questions.hint: Organelles float in it.
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm fills the cell. Organelles are suspended in it and many reactions happen there.

questions.prompt: Which organelle carries out photosynthesis in a plant cell?
questions.hint: It contains the green pigment chlorophyll.
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and turn light, water and carbon dioxide into glucose.
questions.workedExample: Leaf cells have many chloroplasts. Root cells have none.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of ribosomes?
questions.hint: They read instructions copied from DNA.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes join amino acids together to build proteins.

questions.prompt: Which structure controls what enters and leaves a cell?
questions.hint: Every cell has this thin outer layer.
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, so it controls which substances pass through.

questions.prompt: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus. What is a likely benefit?
questions.hint: Think about what the cell must carry.
questions.explanation: Without a nucleus there is more room for hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen.

questions.prompt: Why does a plant cell in pure water not burst, while an animal cell can?
questions.hint: Think about which cell has a rigid outer layer.
questions.explanation: Water enters by osmosis. The strong cell wall resists the pressure, but an animal cell membrane can burst.

questions.prompt: All living things are made of one or more cells.
questions.hint: This is a main idea of cell theory.
questions.explanation: Cell theory says every living thing is made of cells, and new cells come from existing cells.

questions.prompt: Animal cells contain chloroplasts.
questions.hint: Animals do not make food from sunlight.
questions.explanation: Only plant cells and some other organisms such as algae have chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: Bacterial cells do not have a membrane-bound nucleus.
questions.hint: Bacteria are prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells such as bacteria keep their DNA in the cytoplasm, not in a nucleus.

questions.prompt: Put these levels of life in order, smallest first.
questions.hint: Many of one level join to make the next.
questions.explanation: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together as an organ system.

questions.prompt: Put the stages of mitosis in order.
questions.hint: Chromosomes condense, line up, split, then two nuclei form.
questions.explanation: Mitosis runs: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase (remember PMAT).

questions.prompt: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. Find its average speed.

steps.why: Speed is distance per unit time.
km divided by h gives km/h.

questions.hint: Speed = distance ÷ time.
questions.explanation: Average speed = 150 km ÷ 3 h = 50 km/h.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.hint: It is named after a famous scientist.
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). One newton accelerates 1 kg at 1 m/s².

questions.prompt: Which force pulls objects toward the center of the Earth?
questions.hint: It makes a dropped ball fall.
questions.explanation: Gravity is the attraction between masses. Earth's gravity pulls everything toward its center.

questions.prompt: Which force slows down a box sliding across the floor?
questions.hint: Rough surfaces make it stronger.
questions.explanation: Friction acts between touching surfaces and opposes their motion.

questions.prompt: A 10 kg object gets a net force of 20 N. What is its acceleration?
questions.hint: Use a = F ÷ m.
questions.explanation: a = F ÷ m = 20 N ÷ 10 kg = 2 m/s².
questions.workedExample: A 4 kg cart with net force 12 N: a = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 m/s².

questions.prompt: A cyclist rides 36 km in 2 hours. What is the average speed?
questions.hint: Divide distance by time.
questions.explanation: 36 km ÷ 2 h = 18 km/h.

questions.prompt: Which of these has both a size and a direction?
questions.hint: Speed plus a direction.
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector: speed in a given direction. Speed, mass and time have size only.

questions.prompt: Which law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction?
questions.hint: Think of a rocket pushing gas backward.
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: if A pushes on B, then B pushes back on A with an equal force in the opposite direction.

questions.prompt: An object moves in a straight line at constant speed. What is the net force on it?
questions.hint: Think about Newton's first law.
questions.explanation: With no change in velocity there is no acceleration, so the net force is zero.

questions.prompt: An astronaut goes from Earth to the Moon. What happens to their mass?
questions.hint: Mass is the amount of matter, not the pull on it.
questions.explanation: Mass does not change with place. Only weight changes, because the Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's.

questions.prompt: A force can change the speed of an object.
questions.hint: Think of kicking a ball.
questions.explanation: A net force makes an object speed up, slow down or change direction.

questions.prompt: Friction is a force that opposes motion between two surfaces.
questions.hint: Why do your shoes grip the floor?
questions.explanation: Friction acts against the direction of sliding between two touching surfaces.

questions.prompt: Mass and weight are the same thing.
questions.hint: Mass is in kilograms. Weight is a force.
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter (kg). Weight is the pull of gravity on it, measured in newtons.

questions.prompt: In a vacuum, a heavy ball and a light ball fall at the same rate.
questions.hint: Air resistance is missing in a vacuum.
questions.explanation: Without air resistance every object accelerates at the same rate (about 9.8 m/s² on Earth).

questions.prompt: What force gives a 5 kg cart an acceleration of 3 m/s²?
questions.hint: Force = mass × acceleration.
questions.explanation: F = m × a = 5 kg × 3 m/s² = 15 N.

questions.prompt: Put these in order of typical speed, slowest first.
questions.hint: Think of meters per second for each.
questions.explanation: Walking is about 1.4 m/s, cycling about 5 m/s, a highway car about 30 m/s and a jet about 250 m/s.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.hint: Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
questions.explanation: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom: H₂O.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.hint: It comes from the Latin word aurum.
questions.explanation: Gold is Au, from Latin aurum. Ag is silver.

questions.prompt: Which particle in an atom has a negative charge?
questions.hint: It moves around the outside of the nucleus.
questions.explanation: Electrons are negative, protons are positive and neutrons have no charge.

questions.prompt: Which state of matter has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?
questions.hint: Particles are packed tightly and only vibrate.
questions.explanation: In a solid the particles are held in fixed positions, so it keeps its shape and volume.

questions.prompt: How many protons does a carbon atom have?
questions.hint: It is the atomic number of carbon.
questions.explanation: Carbon has atomic number 6, so every carbon atom has 6 protons.

questions.prompt: A solution has a pH of 2. What kind of substance is it?
questions.hint: Compare it with pH 7.
questions.explanation: A pH below 7 is acidic. Pure water is neutral at pH 7, and bases are above 7.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.hint: A new substance is formed.
questions.explanation: Rusting makes iron oxide, a new substance. Melting, boiling and dissolving are physical changes.

questions.prompt: An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.hint: Count the particles in the nucleus.
questions.explanation: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 11 + 12 = 23. This atom is sodium-23.

questions.prompt: Why do the noble gases rarely react with other elements?
questions.hint: Think about the outer electrons.
questions.explanation: Noble gases already have a full outer electron shell, so they have little tendency to gain, lose or share electrons.

questions.prompt: Water is made of the elements hydrogen and oxygen.
questions.hint: Remember H₂O.
questions.explanation: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.prompt: An element is made of only one kind of atom.
questions.hint: Think of pure gold or pure oxygen.
questions.explanation: Every atom in an element has the same number of protons.

questions.prompt: Salt dissolved in water is a compound.
questions.hint: The salt can be recovered by evaporating the water.
questions.explanation: Salt water is a mixture (a solution). Salt itself is a compound, but it is not chemically joined to the water.

questions.prompt: Protons and neutrons are found in the nucleus of an atom.
questions.hint: The electrons are the ones outside.
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons. Electrons move around it.

questions.prompt: Balance the equation H₂ + O₂ → H₂O

steps.why: Count the atoms on each side.
Never change the little numbers in a formula.
Put 2 before H₂ to balance hydrogen.

questions.hint: Balance oxygen first, then hydrogen.
questions.explanation: Put 2 before H₂O to get 2 oxygen atoms, then 2 before H₂ to get 4 hydrogen atoms. Both sides now balance.

questions.prompt: Put these states of matter in order of particle energy, lowest first.
questions.hint: Heating moves matter up the list.
questions.explanation: Heating takes a substance from solid to liquid to gas, and extreme heat can make a plasma.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.hint: It is the smallest planet.
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, followed by Venus, Earth and Mars.

questions.prompt: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.hint: Earth does it once in about 24 hours.
questions.explanation: Earth spins on its axis about once a day, so each place turns toward and away from the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.hint: It is about 78% of the air.
questions.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.prompt: What causes the seasons on Earth?
questions.hint: Earth's axis is not straight up and down.
questions.explanation: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.5°, so each hemisphere gets more direct sunlight at different times of year.

questions.prompt: Which layer of the Earth is liquid metal?
questions.hint: It lies between the mantle and the inner core.
questions.explanation: The outer core is liquid iron and nickel. The inner core is solid because of the huge pressure.

questions.prompt: Which type of rock forms when magma cools and hardens?
questions.hint: The name comes from a Latin word for fire.
questions.explanation: Igneous rock forms from cooled magma or lava. Granite and basalt are examples.

questions.prompt: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.hint: Light is fast, but the Sun is very far away.
questions.explanation: The Sun is about 150 million km away. Light travels there in about 500 seconds, or 8 minutes.

questions.prompt: What causes a lunar eclipse?
questions.hint: Think about whose shadow falls on whom.
questions.explanation: In a lunar eclipse Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, so Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

questions.prompt: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon from Earth?
questions.hint: Compare how long it takes to spin and to orbit.
questions.explanation: The Moon takes the same time to spin once as to orbit Earth once (tidal locking), so the same face points at us.

questions.prompt: The Sun is a star.
questions.hint: It makes its own light and heat.
questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the center of our solar system.

questions.prompt: Earth takes about 365 days to orbit the Sun once.
questions.hint: That is the length of a year.
questions.explanation: One orbit takes about 365.25 days, which is why we have a leap year every four years.

questions.prompt: The Moon makes its own light.
questions.hint: Where does moonlight come from?
questions.explanation: The Moon reflects sunlight. It does not produce light of its own.

questions.prompt: Summer happens because Earth is closer to the Sun.
questions.hint: Both hemispheres cannot have summer at the same time.
questions.explanation: Seasons come from Earth's tilt. Earth is actually slightly closer to the Sun in January.

questions.prompt: Sunlight travels 150 million km at 300 000 km/s. How long does it take?
questions.hint: Time = distance ÷ speed.
questions.explanation: 150 000 000 ÷ 300 000 = 500 seconds, which is about 8.3 minutes.

questions.prompt: Put these planets in order, closest to the Sun first.
questions.hint: Hotter planets are nearer to the Sun.
questions.explanation: The order from the Sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, then Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

questions.prompt: Step only on living things.
questions.hint: Living things grow, reproduce and are made of cells.
questions.explanation: Trees, mushrooms, frogs, bacteria and moss are alive and made of cells. Rocks, sand, water, cars and flames are not.

questions.prompt: Step only on forces.
questions.hint: A force is a push or a pull.
questions.explanation: Gravity, friction, air resistance, tension and magnetic force are pushes or pulls. Mass, speed, distance, time and energy are not forces.

questions.prompt: Step only on chemical elements.
questions.hint: An element has only one kind of atom.
questions.explanation: Oxygen, iron, gold, carbon and helium are elements. Water, salt, carbon dioxide, sugar and rust are compounds made of different atoms.

questions.prompt: Step only on planets of our Solar System.
questions.hint: There are eight planets. Pluto was reclassified.
questions.explanation: The eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Pluto and Ceres are dwarf planets, the Moon is a moon, the Sun is a star.
